chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Burayd ibn Mu'awiya said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who freed his slave conditionally upon his death (mudabbir), who was a wealthy merchant. The freed slave bought a female slave, and then the freed slave died before his master. He said, and he (the Imam) said: 'I see that all the wealth or possessions left by the mudabbir belong to the one who freed him. And I see that the mother of his child (umm walad) belongs to the one who freed him. And I see that her children are also mudabbarun, in the manner of their father. So when the one who freed their father dies, they become free.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَد: A female slave who bears her master's child
key_terms.دَبَّرَ: To conditionally free a slave upon the master's death
key_terms.مُدَبَّر: A slave conditionally freed upon the master's death

ai.seo_question: What happens to the property and slaves of a mudabbir who dies before his master?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, clarifying that the 'mudabbir' retains full ownership of his acquired property and offspring, which revert to the original master upon the mudabbir's predecease. This ruling underscores the conditional nature of the emancipation, where the slave's status as a dependent heir is suspended until the master's death, at which point the children inherit the father's freedom. The hadith highlights the precise legal mechanics of conditional manumission in early Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the mudabbir's personal estate and his eventual liberation.
